cve_summary: drivers/net/ieee802154/atusb.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x before 4.9.6 interacts incorrectly with the CONFIG_VMAP_STACK option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash or memory corruption) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of more than one virtual page for a DMA scatterlist.
commit_message:
ieee802154: atusb: do not use the stack for buffers to make them DMA able

From 4.9 we should really avoid using the stack here as this will not be DMA
able on various platforms. This changes the buffers already being present in
time of 4.9 being released. This should go into stable as well.

Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Stefan Schmidt <stefan@osg.samsung.com>
Signed-off-by: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtmann.org>
docstring:
Summary: This code fragment defines several functions for controlling USB communication with an ATUSB device, including reading and writing registers, sending commands, and managing errors.

Parameters: 
atusb (struct atusb *): pointer to the ATUSB device structure  
pipe (unsigned int): the USB pipe to use for communication  
request (__u8): the specific request code to send  
requesttype (__u8): the type of request (device, interface, endpoint)  
value (__u16): a value associated with the request  
index (__u16): an index or offset for the request  
data (void *): pointer to data to send or receive  
size (__u16): size of the data buffer  
timeout (int): timeout for the operation in milliseconds  

Returns: int: the result of the operation, with negative values indicating errors  

Logic: The code manages USB control messages through the `atusb_control_msg` function, which checks for existing errors before proceeding with the request. If an error occurs during the USB operation, it logs the error and stores it in the device structure. The `atusb_command`, `atusb_write_reg`, and `atusb_read_reg` functions utilize this control message function to perform specific tasks, such as sending commands or reading/writing register values. The `atusb_write_subreg` function modifies specific bits of a register based on a mask, while `atusb_get_and_clear_error` retrieves and resets the error state. Additionally, the code includes definitions for maximum payload sizes and a macro for accessing ATUSB structures in socket buffers.
extraction_reason: vulnerable-side scope spans 6 top-level constructs (functions/declarations), not a single function
